convert.title: Make any .3mf U1-ready
convert.intro: Drop a .3mf from MakerWorld, Bambu Studio, PrusaSlicer, Orca or Creality Print — get back a U1-ready file: the foreign profile swapped for the real Snapmaker U1 profile, painted multicolor mapped to the U1's 4 slots, colors preserved. Runs entirely in your browser — nothing is uploaded.
convert.livePreview: · Live colored preview before you download
convert.tip: Tip: the <link>browser extension</link> does this right on the MakerWorld/Printables download page.
convert.preserveDesc: Keeps the creator's layer height, walls, infill & speeds — swaps only the printer to your U1. Best fidelity to the original. Re-slice in Snapmaker Orca.
convert.stampDesc: Replaces all settings with our U1 profile ({nozzle, number} nozzle) + your colors. Most consistent results.
convert.keepAllLabel: This file has {count, plural, one {# color} other {# colors}} — more than the U1's 4 slots. Keep every one of them in the file and choose which head each loads on in Snapmaker Orca, instead of merging or mixing.
convert.keepAllDesc: Nothing is merged, mixed or renumbered — the palette arrives exactly as the author left it. The U1 prints 4 filaments per plate, so Orca will ask you to map them before it slices.
convert.brandSourceDesc: Leaves each slot named as the original file had it (e.g. “Bambu PLA Basic”). No change.
convert.brandGenericDesc: Renames every slot to “Generic <material>”, which any slicer can resolve.
convert.brandSnapmakerDesc: Renames each slot to Snapmaker's own preset where one exists, and Generic where it doesn't (there's no Snapmaker PC, for instance). Useful when a model repository asks for Generic or vendor presets rather than another printer's brand.
convert.nozzleDerivedNote: Only the {tested, number} mm profile is a real export from a U1 that has actually printed. {nozzle, number} mm adapts it by nozzle ratio: your file gets the right nozzle identity and extrusion widths scaled to match, but nobody has print-tested this profile. Check the first layer before a long print.
convert.swapPausesDesc: This file changes color by height and has {count, plural, one {# color} other {# colors}}. Keep them all with M600 spool-swap pauses instead of merging to 4.
convert.swapPausesNote: The U1 will pause at each swap so you change the spool by hand. Verify the plan before a long print.
convert.vlhDesc: This file uses variable layer height — it carries over either way. By default we turn the prime tower off and use normal supports, because Snapmaker Orca errors on variable layers + a prime tower / tree supports. Tick to keep the creator's prime tower & supports.
convert.vlhNote: Only if your Orca build slices variable layers with a prime tower — otherwise leave this off, or the file may fail to slice.
convert.importCurrentDesc: Strips the profile; set colors in Orca.
convert.genericStripDesc: Opens in any slicer / any printer — colors kept, U1 profile removed.
convert.doneGeneric: Done — vendor profile stripped. Opens in any slicer, colors kept.
convert.targetKeepNote: Rewrites the file's printer profile to {name} and remaps your colors to its slots.
convert.targetGenericNote: {name} uses a different slicer format — saved as a clean Generic 3MF you open and assign to {name}. Geometry carries over; painted multicolor may need re-applying in {name}'s slicer.
convert.doneRetarget: Done — retargeted for {name}. Re-slice in that printer's slicer.
convert.doneRetargetGeneric: Done — saved as a Generic 3MF. Open it in {name}'s slicer and pick {name}; geometry is preserved, but re-check painted colors — multicolor may not carry across ecosystems.
convert.batchDesc: Have a whole folder of multicolor .3mf files? Convert them all to U1-ready files at once — each keeps its creator's print settings — and get back a ZIP.

Mixing can't manufacture a color that isn't one of your 4 heads, so they'll shift a lot (e.g.). It suits blended palettes (skin tones, gradients); a set of saturated, distinct colors like this can't be faked with 4 filaments. Pick the 4 that matter most below, or expect visible shifts on the rest.

convert.lopsidedTip: Some mixes are lopsided (e.g. 80/20). They're printed with ordered dithering so they blend evenly rather than banding — but for the finest blend on these, lower the mixed-color layer height below, or nudge the ratio toward 50/50 (or pick a main color closer to that shade).
convert.mlhNoteSame: Mix prints at the model's normal layer height.
convert.mlhNoteSet: Re-slices just the mixed regions at this height — more, thinner layers there (longer print).

convert.diffKeptAll: Kept all {count, plural, one {# filament} other {# filaments}} untouched — map them to heads in Snapmaker Orca

convert.subdivideDesc: On: the U1 splits each layer into thinner sub-layers inside mixed areas, so blends look smoother — especially on top-facing surfaces. Off: fewer filament changes → faster prints and less purge waste, but slightly coarser mixes. We leave it on because a real test print looked noticeably better with it; turn it off if print time or filament waste matters more to you.

convert.warnMixedFilaments: This file mixes {families} filaments. On the U1’s prime/wipe tower these can fail to bond to each other (e.g. PLA won’t stick to PETG → "spaghetti"). In Orca, set the prime tower’s filament to your main material instead of "Default".
convert.warnPaintedEdits: Colors are painted onto the mesh. After converting, don’t use "Split to objects/parts" or the Cut tool in Orca — those drop painted colors.
convert.warnOverFourByLayer: {count, plural, one {# color} other {# colors}} — more than the U1’s 4 slots. Turn on the M600 spool-swap pauses below to keep all {count}; leave them off and the least-used colors merge into their nearest match.
convert.warnOverFourMerge: {count, plural, one {# color} other {# colors}} — more than the U1’s 4 slots. Turn on Full Spectrum below to keep all {count}, reproduced by mixing your 4 filaments; leave it off and the least-used colors merge into their nearest match.
convert.warnOverhangYes: Steep overhangs detected (~{percent}% of the surface). Supports are recommended — the converter keeps your source file’s support setting, so if it didn’t already have them, turn Supports on in Snapmaker Orca before slicing.
convert.warnOverhangNo: No significant overhangs detected — this model likely prints without supports. The converter keeps whatever support setting your source file had.
convert.warnTooBig: This model is {x}×{y}×{z} mm — larger than the Snapmaker U1’s {maxXY}×{maxXY}×{maxZ} mm build volume. It may not fit; rotate or rescale in your slicer.

convert.customFsDesc: Reproduce this model’s colors as blends of your 4 loaded filaments — at any color count. Set your filaments below (defaults to CMYK); each painted color becomes its closest mix.

convert.blendTip: For clean blends: Full Spectrum fakes colors by stacking ultra-thin layers, so translucent filaments (light diffuses across layers) blend far better than opaque ones, which tend to show fine stripes — most on flat top surfaces and shallow slopes. Keep the mix layer height ≤ 0.1 mm and the effect stays invisible at arm’s length.

help.title: Help & FAQ
help.intro: Everything about converting files for the Snapmaker U1, the library, and your account. Can't find it? <link>Ask us</link>.
help.outro: Still stuck or have an idea? <link>Send feedback</link> — we read everything.

items.q: What does the converter actually do?
items.a: Multicolor files from MakerWorld, Bambu, Printables and Thingiverse are sliced for other printers (usually Bambu's AMS). The converter swaps the foreign printer profile for the real Snapmaker U1 profile, maps the painted colors onto the U1's 4 slots, keeps the original colors, and fixes the filament-change pauses.

items.q: Why not just use File → Import in the slicer?
items.a: For Bambu Lab files with 4 colors or fewer, importing into Snapmaker Orca often does carry the colors over — for that case it's fine. The converter matters when Import falls short: PrusaSlicer and Creality files import as 'geometry only' and the painted colors are dropped; the prime tower keeps non-U1 settings (a common cause of multicolor failures); the source printer's profile and speeds come along; files with more than 4 colors aren't reduced or mixed; and by-layer color files don't get the spool-swap pauses. BedReady handles all of that in one click and shows a 'what changed' report.

items.q: Is my file uploaded anywhere?
items.a: No. The converter runs entirely in your browser — your file never leaves your device. There's an optional server converter for very large files; even that processes in memory and stores nothing.

items.q: Which files does it accept?
items.a: .3mf files from MakerWorld, Bambu Studio, PrusaSlicer, OrcaSlicer (including the Snapmaker Orca fork), and Creality Print. Plain STL/OBJ have no color data, so there's nothing to convert.

items.q: Do I need to do anything after converting?
items.a: Yes — open the converted file in Snapmaker Orca and re-slice it. The converter sets up the profile, colors, and pauses; Orca generates the actual G-code.

items.q: It looks a bit messy in Orca — is the conversion broken?
items.a: Usually not. Floating bits or gaps almost always come from the original model (common with HueForge-style or hollowed designs), not the conversion — the geometry is passed through untouched.

items.q: What do the three buttons do?
items.a: Clean for U1 is the main one: the real U1 profile plus your colors mapped to the 4 slots. Import to current printer just strips the foreign profile so you pick colors in your own slicer. Geometry .STL exports the shape only, without colors.

items.q: Big file — why did the preview disappear?
items.a: For very large models we skip the live 3D preview to stay responsive — conversion still works on the full model. If the browser struggles, an optional convert-on-our-server button appears.

items.q: My file has more than 4 colors — what happens?
items.a: The U1 has 4 slots, so the converter reduces to the 4 closest colors by default. Or turn on Full Spectrum to approximate the extra colors by mixing your 4 physical filaments.

items.q: What is Full Spectrum / color mixing?
items.a: It dithers your 4 loaded filaments to fake additional colors, so a 6- or 8-color model can print with just 4 spools. You choose the 4 physical colors and the converter computes the mixes. It works best for areas of solid color; very fine detail mixes less cleanly.

items.q: Can I choose which slot each color loads into?
items.a: Yes — use the ◀ ▶ buttons under each slot to rearrange them to match how your filaments are physically loaded. The print stays identical; only the slot positions change.

items.q: What are the spool-swap pauses?
items.a: For files that change color by layer height, the converter inserts pauses so the U1 stops and lets you swap filament by hand at each change. You'll see the swap plan after converting.

items.q: The file has several parts — can I see them separately?
items.a: Yes. When a file has multiple parts or plates, the preview lets you step through them by plate, by part, or all at once.

items.q: What is Split into separate files?
items.a: For multi-part files, it downloads a .zip with each part as its own single-plate file — re-centered on the bed and converted independently, so each file's 4 slots hold only that part's colors. Print them one at a time, swapping filament between parts.

items.q: What does the Verified on U1 badge mean?
items.a: It means a file's print profile has been confirmed to actually print correctly on a Snapmaker U1, backed by a photo of the real print. That's the whole point of BedReady — files you can trust to work, not just convert.

items.q: How do I share a file?
items.a: Upload it, or link to it on another site. Add a cover photo, a category, and tags. If you attach a tested profile, include a proof-of-print photo. Submissions are reviewed before they go public.

items.q: Browsing — categories, tags, search?
items.a: The library filters by category (the same top-level set as Printables and MakerWorld), tags, and color count, with search and a Most liked sort.

items.q: Likes, comments, and makes?
items.a: Signed-in makers can like a design, comment, and post a make (a photo of your own print of it). Your activity shows on your public maker profile.

items.q: A file is broken or breaks the rules — what do I do?
items.a: Use the Report this file link on the design page (no sign-in needed). We review every report.

items.q: What about licenses?
items.a: Each file shows its license. See the licenses page for what each one allows. Always respect the original creator's terms.

items.q: Is there a browser extension?
items.a: Yes — it adds a Make U1-ready option right on the download page at MakerWorld, Bambu, Printables and Thingiverse. Like the site, it converts in your browser and uploads nothing.

items.q: How do I sign in?
items.a: Passwordless — enter your email on the login page and click the magic link we send. No password to remember.

items.q: Notifications — can I turn off emails?
items.a: Yes. You get an in-app bell for activity on your files, plus optional emails. Toggle the emails off anytime on your account page.

items.q: Change my display name or avatar?
items.a: On your account page — set a display name, bio, and avatar. This is what other makers see.

items.q: Is it free? What about my data?
items.a: Yes, free. We collect as little as possible and never sell your data — see the privacy policy.

items.q: Is BedReady affiliated with Snapmaker?
items.a: No. It's an independent project, not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Snapmaker, Bambu Lab, or MakerWorld.

extension.title: BedReady browser extension
extension.intro: Convert multicolor .3mf files to print on the Snapmaker U1 right from the download page on MakerWorld, Bambu, Printables & Thingiverse. It runs entirely in your browser — nothing is uploaded. Available for Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Safari.
extension.firefoxPending: Pending review on Firefox Add-ons. Until it’s approved you can load the .zip manually with the steps below.
extension.safariPending: In review on the Mac App Store — the install button appears here once it’s approved.
extension.safariNote: On Safari, open the toolbar popup and drop a .3mf in, or use the “→ U1” button on model pages. Safari doesn’t support auto-convert-on-download like Chrome and Firefox.
extension.prefer: Prefer not to install anything? The <link>web converter</link> does the same thing — just drag a file in.

licenses.title: License guide
licenses.intro: 3D models are shared under licenses that say what you're allowed to do — print, modify, or sell. Here's what the common ones mean. When you upload, pick the license that matches how you want your work used. When you download, always respect the creator's license.
licenses.note: Note: BedReady aggregates some files as links to their original source — in those cases the creator's license on the source site always applies. This page is a plain-language summary, not legal advice. For full terms see <link>creativecommons.org</link>.

items.name: Public Domain (CC0)
items.detail: The creator waived all rights. You can use, modify, remix, and sell prints with no attribution. The most permissive option.

items.name: Attribution (CC BY)
items.summary: Do anything — just credit the creator.
items.detail: Use, modify, remix, and sell — including commercially — as long as you give credit to the original designer.

items.name: Attribution-ShareAlike (CC BY-SA)
items.summary: Credit + share remixes under the same license.
items.detail: Like CC BY, but anything you make from it (remixes, modifications) must be shared under this same license. Commercial use allowed.

items.name: Attribution-NonCommercial (CC BY-NC)
items.detail: Use, modify, and remix with credit — but NOT for commercial purposes. You can't sell the prints or the files.

items.name: Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike
items.detail: Personal use only, must credit, and any remixes must use this same license. Common on MakerWorld/Printables.

items.name: Attribution-NoDerivatives (CC BY-ND)
items.detail: You can use and share the file as-is (with credit), but you may NOT modify or remix it. Commercial use of the unchanged file is allowed.

items.name: All Rights Reserved
items.summary: Print for yourself; nothing else without permission.
items.detail: The creator keeps all rights. Typically you may print it for personal use, but not redistribute, modify, or sell without explicit permission.

licenses.ourCodeBody: The converter is open source under the MIT license — <link>github.com/BedReady/bedready</link>. That is also how the “nothing is uploaded” claim is checkable rather than merely asserted: the conversion path is in the repository, and you can read it. The licenses above are about the models people share, not about this software.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: BedReady is an independent project that helps makers convert and share 3D-print files for any printer — it began with the Snapmaker U1 and now covers every printer its file checker recognises. This policy covers both the website (bedready.io) and the BedReady browser extension (Chrome, Firefox, and Safari). We aim to collect as little as possible and never sell your data.
privacy.extIntro: The extension collects no data and sends nothing to any server. Conversion happens entirely in your browser — your files are never uploaded. Permissions are used only to provide the single feature (converting a downloaded .3mf for the Snapmaker U1):
extBullets: downloads — to read the .3mf you're downloading and save the converted file back to your device.
notifications — to let you know when a conversion finishes.

site access (MakerWorld, Bambu/bblmw, Printables, Thingiverse) — the in-page helper runs only on those model sites to detect a .3mf and offer conversion. It does nothing on any other site, and reads nothing beyond the file you choose to convert.
privacy.extNote: No browsing history, analytics, or personal data is collected by the extension.
privacy.siteIntro: The in-browser converter at bedready.io also runs locally — files dropped there are not uploaded. Beyond that, the site stores only what you actively provide:
siteBullets: Account — if you sign in, your email address (for magic-link login, via Supabase) and a profile (display name, optional bio and avatar).
Content you post — designs/files, comments, «makes» (photos), likes, and reports. These are public by nature of the site.

Optional server converter — if you choose the optional «convert on our server» path, the file is processed in memory and not stored; we keep only metadata (file sizes, source host, a salted hash of your IP, timing) to monitor cost and abuse. Reports also store a salted IP hash.

Analytics — privacy-friendly, aggregate usage analytics (Vercel Analytics); no advertising trackers. So we can tell which sites and posts bring people here, your browser also stores the referring site’s domain (the domain only, never the page address) and any utm_ tags in the link you followed, for 30 days. It contains no identifier of any kind, so it cannot follow you anywhere, and it is attached only to anonymous counts.
Email notifications — if enabled, we email you (via Resend) when someone interacts with your files. You can turn these off anytime on your account page.
privacy.cookies: Only an essential authentication session cookie when you're signed in. No advertising or cross-site tracking cookies.
privacy.choices: You can edit or delete your content, opt out of notification emails, and request account deletion. We don't sell or share personal data with third parties for their own use.
privacy.contact: Questions? Reach us via the <link>feedback form</link>.
privacy.footer: Independent project — not affiliated with Snapmaker, Bambu Lab, MakerWorld, Printables, or Thingiverse.

Pick a filament below and install it in one click, or download and import it. Free, in your browser, nothing uploaded.
orcaPage.faq1q: How do I add an OrcaSlicer filament profile to Snapmaker Orca?
orcaPage.faq1a: Pick a filament below. On macOS and Windows, browsers block writing into the config folder (~/Library and %APPDATA%), so the profile downloads and you import it in Orca: File → Import → Import Presets (or drag the file onto the window) — it appears in the filament dropdown immediately, no restart. One-click direct install works on Linux (Chrome/Edge), and the desktop app installs directly on any OS. Make sure the Snapmaker U1 is your selected printer.

orcaPage.faq3q: Are these tuned for the Snapmaker U1?
orcaPage.faq3a: Each profile is set to be compatible with the Snapmaker U1 so it shows up in the filament dropdown. Temperatures and basic flow carry over as a solid starting point; printer-specific calibration (pressure advance, flow ratio) is worth checking for your setup.
orcaPage.faq4a: No. The whole thing runs in your browser — the profile file is written to (or downloaded onto) your own computer. Nothing is uploaded and there's no account.

OrcaSlicer, Snapmaker Orca and all brand and product names are trademarks of their respective owners. Filament profiles are derived from the open-source OrcaSlicer project and adapted for the Snapmaker U1 — provided as a starting point, so verify settings for your printer.

Where the .3mf is hosted here, our server re-downloads it and inspects it for a genuine slicer profile, and records which printer that profile is for — a maker cannot grant that to themselves, and neither can an admin. A print photo is supplied by the maker and confirmed by a moderator, who checks it is a photograph and not a render. A listing that links to a file hosted elsewhere can never have the file check, because there is no file here to read; it can still have a confirmed print photo.

calibrate.title: Filament calibration card
calibrate.intro: Photographic relief printing predicts color from one number per filament — TD, how far light travels into the plastic before it is blocked. It cannot be looked up: it changes with pigment, so it differs between brands and between colors of the same brand. This prints a card that measures it.
calibrate.oneSpool: One spool per card. The U1 changes filament by height rather than by area, so every pad above the base is the same color — calibrating four spools means four prints.
calibrate.backingHelp: Dark and fully opaque works best — it is the color that has to stop showing through.
calibrate.testHelp: The spool you want a real TD for.
calibrate.layerHelp: Use the same layer height you print reliefs at, or the number will not transfer.
calibrate.warnNoContrast: The two colors are identical, so nothing will show through and the card cannot measure anything. Pick a backing that contrasts with the filament under test.
calibrate.warnLowContrast: Those two colors are too close for the card to measure anything — the backing has to stop showing through, and it can only do that against a filament it visibly differs from. Use a dark, opaque backing (near-black works best).
calibrate.warnHex: Enter both colors as 6-digit hex, e.g. #101010.
calibrate.errBuild: Those settings cannot produce a measurable card. Try more steps or a thicker backing.
calibrate.built: Card is {x} × {y} mm with {pads} pads, from {thin} mm up to {thick} mm of the filament under test.
calibrate.loadOrder: Load the backing in head 1 and the filament under test in head 2 — the card swaps between them by height.
calibrate.how1: Print the card flat, with no supports. It is a thin plate, so it takes minutes rather than hours.
calibrate.how2: Photograph it straight on under even, indirect light. Avoid glare and colored lamps — the measurement is the color, so the light matters.
calibrate.how3: Note the color at the center of each pad, plus the bare backing and the thickest pad.
calibrate.how4: Those readings give TD. Feeding them back in automatically is not built yet — send the photo and I will fit it by hand until it is.
calibrate.beta: Experimental. The card and the maths are tested; what has not been tested is a real print, which is exactly what this is for.
